senses.gloss:
Goloka
(‘the world of light’)
------------------------------------------
What happens to the person after the death of the physical body has been the subject of discussion and conjecture in many religions of the world. In हिन्दुइस्म्, especially in its mythological literature, some special lokas or worlds (special regions of existence) are mentioned to where extremely fortunate souls, deeply pious and spiritual persons, go after their exit from this mundane existence. In the Vaiṣṇavite works, वैकुण्ठ and गोलोक are prominently mentioned. The former seems to be a more ancient concept. As the cult of कृष्ण developed, superseding the cult of विष्णु wherein कृष्ण was considered as only one of the incarnations of विष्णु, कृष्ण was projected as the main cult-deity, Supreme ब्रह्मन् in his personal aspect. Even विष्णु in वैकुण्ठ and शिव in his कैलास were pictured as inferior to कृष्ण and as his lower manifestations.
As per this कृष्ण cult, he, the Supreme ब्रह्मन् or the Absolute, lives in गोलोक (also called Mahāvaikuṇṭha and Vṛndāvana) which is his eternal abode. ‘Goloka’ means ‘the world of light’ and not the world of cows as is often mistaken. This light is all-pervading and extremely beautiful. It is the highest world below which are situated other worlds like वैकुण्ठ, कैलास, स्वर्ग (heaven), martya (world of mortals) and पाताल (nether-world). Its extent is 900 million square yojanas (1 yojana = 15 kms. or 9 miles). It is full of brilliant light, precious stones and other riches. Even the great yogis cannot perceive it, even in their द्रेअम्स्! However the devotees of कृष्ण have access to it. Those who go there and live eternally, will never suffer from any disease or disability.
